question_text: The functional group, which is found in amino acid is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amino acids are organic compounds containing both a carboxylic acid ($\text{-COOH}$) group and an amino ($\text{-NH}_2$) group.

question_text: RNA is different from DNA because RNA contains:
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose as its pentose sugar and uracil (in place of thymine found in DNA) as a pyrimidine base.

question_text: Complete hydrolysis of cellulose gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cellulose is a linear polysaccharide of $\beta$-D-glucose units; complete hydrolysis yields D-glucose: $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5)_n + n\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow n\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$.

question_text: The reason for double helical structure of DNA is operation of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: The two antiparallel polynucleotide strands of DNA are held together in a double helix by specific intermolecular hydrogen bonding between complementary base pairs ($\text{A}=\text{T}$ and $\text{G}\equiv\text{C}$).

question_text: Which one of the following statements is false?
options: Raoult's law states that the vapour pressure of a component over a solution is proportional to its mole fraction
Two sucrose solutions of same molality prepared in different solvents will have the same freezing point depression
The correct order of osmotic pressure for $0.01\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of each compound is $\text{BaCl}_2 > \text{KCl} > \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} > \text{sucrose}$
The osmotic pressure $(\pi) = MRT$, where $M$ is the molarity of the solution
subject: Chemistry
solution: Freezing point depression is given by $\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m$, where $K_f$ is the molal depression constant characteristic of the solvent. Different solvents have different $K_f$ values, so equimolal solutions in different solvents will not have the same freezing point depression.

question_text: Which base is present in RNA but not in DNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil, whereas DNA contains thymine instead of uracil.

question_text: In both DNA and RNA, heterocyclic base and phosphate ester linkages are at:
options: $\text{C}_5'$ and $\text{C}_1'$ respectively of the sugar molecule
$\text{C}_2'$ and $\text{C}_5'$ respectively of the sugar molecule
$\text{C}_1'$ and $\text{C}_5'$ respectively of the sugar molecule
$\text{C}_5'$ and $\text{C}_2'$ respectively of the sugar molecule
subject: Chemistry
solution: In a nucleotide unit of both DNA and RNA, the nitrogenous heterocyclic base is attached to the $\text{C}_1'$ carbon via an $N$-glycosidic linkage, while the phosphate group is esterified at the $\text{C}_5'$ carbon of the pentose sugar.

question_text: The term anomers of glucose refers to:
options: isomers of glucose that differ in configurations at carbons one and four ($\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-4$)
isomers of glucose that differ in configuration at carbon one ($\text{C}-1$)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Anomers ($\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose) are cyclic diastereomeric hemiacetals that differ in configuration solely at the anomeric carbon ($\text{C}-1$).

question_text: The pyrimidine bases present in DNA are:
subject: Chemistry
solution: DNA contains two purine bases (adenine and guanine) and two pyrimidine bases (cytosine and thymine).

question_text: The secondary structure of a protein refers to:
options: fixed configuration of the polypeptide backbone
subject: Chemistry
solution: Secondary structure of proteins refers to the regular local folding of the polypeptide backbone into $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet conformations stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

question_text: $\alpha$-D-(+)-glucose and $\beta$-D-(+)-glucose are:
subject: Chemistry
solution: $\alpha$-D-(+)-glucose and $\beta$-D-(+)-glucose differ in the orientation of the $-\text{OH}$ group at the $\text{C}-1$ hemiacetal carbon and are therefore anomers.

question_text: The two functional groups present in a typical carbohydrate are:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Carbohydrates are optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones, so they contain hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) and carbonyl ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$) functional groups.

question_text: Biuret test is not given by:
subject: Chemistry
solution: The Biuret test detects peptide/amide ($-\text{CONH}-$) linkages (present in proteins, polypeptides, and heated urea) and is not given by carbohydrates.

question_text: The presence or absence of hydroxyl group on which carbon atom of sugar differentiates RNA and DNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose (which has an $-\text{OH}$ group at $\text{C}-2$), whereas DNA contains $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose (which lacks an $-\text{OH}$ group at the $2^{\text{nd}}$ carbon).

question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: All amino acids except lysine are optically active
All amino acids are optically active
All amino acids except glycine are optically active
All amino acids except glutamic acid are optically active
subject: Chemistry
solution: In glycine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$), the $\alpha$-carbon is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms and is achiral; all other naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids have a chiral $\alpha$-carbon and are optically active.

question_text: Which of the following compounds can be detected by Molisch's test?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Molisch's test is a general confirmatory test for all carbohydrates (sugars), producing a characteristic purple/violet ring at the junction of the sugar + $\alpha$-naphthol solution and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

question_text: All of the following statements apply to proteins except:
options: Proteins generally have no definite melting point
Proteins can only contain the elements $\text{C}, \text{H}, \text{O}$ and $\text{N}$
subject: Chemistry
solution: In addition to $\text{C}, \text{H}, \text{O}$, and $\text{N}$, proteins also contain sulphur (e.g., in cysteine and methionine) and sometimes phosphorus or metal ions. Thus, statement (D) is false.

question_text: Amylopectin is a polymer of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylopectin is a branched-chain polysaccharide component of starch composed of $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ linear and $\alpha(1 \to 6)$ branching glycosidic linkages.

question_text: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide because the anomeric carbons of both $\alpha$-D-glucose ($\text{C}_1$) and $\beta$-D-fructose ($\text{C}_2$) are locked in the glycosidic linkage.

question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: RNA controls the synthesis of proteins.
The sugar present in DNA is D-(-)-2-deoxyribose.
DNA mainly occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell.
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA molecules (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) directly control and carry out protein synthesis in the cell (note: the official answer key for the printed variant lists B).

question_text: Synthesis of each molecule of glucose in photosynthesis involves:
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the Calvin cycle, fixing $6\text{ CO}_2$ molecules to synthesize $1$ molecule of glucose requires $18\text{ ATP}$ and $12\text{ NADPH}$ molecules.

question_text: Which of the following structures represents thymine?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Thymine is 5-methyluracil (5-methylpyrimidine-2,4-dione), corresponding to structure (D).

question_text: Natural glucose is termed D-glucose because:
options: $-\text{OH}$ on the second carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection
$-\text{OH}$ on the sixth carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection
$-\text{OH}$ on the fifth carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the Fischer projection of an aldohexose, the D-configuration is assigned when the $-\text{OH}$ group on the highest-numbered chiral carbon ($\text{C}-5$) lies on the right-hand side.

question_text: Glycosidic linkage is actually an:
subject: Chemistry
solution: A glycosidic linkage joins two monosaccharide units through an oxygen atom ($\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{C}$), which is chemically an ether (acetal) bond.

question_text: Among the following vitamins the one whose deficiency causes rickets (bone deficiency) is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes rickets (bone deformities in children) and osteomalacia (soft bones and joint pain in adults).

question_text: Which one of the following bases is not present in DNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine; quinoline is a bicyclic aromatic nitrogen heterocycle not present in nucleic acids.

question_text: Which of the following will not show mutarotation?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose lacks a free hemiacetal/hemiketal group, so its rings cannot open in aqueous solution to interconvert between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ anomers; hence it does not exhibit mutarotation.

question_text: The reason for double helical structure of DNA is the operation of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Specific hydrogen bonding between purine and pyrimidine base pairs ($\text{A}-\text{T}$ and $\text{G}-\text{C}$) stabilizes the double-helical structure of DNA.

question_text: Which of the vitamins given below is water soluble?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and B-complex vitamins are water-soluble, whereas Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble.

question_text: Complete hydrolysis of starch gives:
options: Galactose and fructose in equimolar amounts
Glucose and galactose in equimolar amounts
Glucose and fructose in equimolar amounts
subject: Chemistry
solution: Starch is a homopolymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose (composed of amylose and amylopectin); complete hydrolysis yields D-glucose only.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I:
A. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Galactose
B. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\beta$-Glucose
C. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Fructose
D. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Ribose

List-II:
I. Functional isomers
II. Homologues
III. Anomers
IV. Epimers
subject: Chemistry

question_text: $\text{Dipeptide (Asn-Ser)} + \text{Ac}_2\text{O (Excess)} \xrightarrow{\text{Et}_3\text{N}} \text{Product}$
options: Monoacetylated at the N-terminal amino group only
Diacetylated at the N-terminal amino group ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$) and the Serine side-chain hydroxyl group ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$)
Triacetylated including the Asn side-chain amide nitrogen
O-acetylated only at the Serine hydroxyl group
subject: Chemistry
solution: Under $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}/\text{Et}_3\text{N}$, both the nucleophilic N-terminal $-\text{NH}_2$ group of Asn and the primary alcoholic $-\text{OH}$ group of Ser undergo acetylation, whereas the resonance-stabilised amide $-\text{CONH}_2$ nitrogen of Asn is not acetylated.

question_text: Accumulation of which of the following molecules in the muscles occurs as a result of vigorous exercise?
subject: Chemistry
solution: During vigorous exercise, oxygen supply to skeletal muscles becomes insufficient, causing anaerobic glycolysis of glucose/pyruvate into L-lactic acid, which accumulates and leads to muscle fatigue.

question_text:
Match List-I (Vitamin) with List-II (Name):
List-I: A. Vitamin $\text{B}_1$, B. Vitamin $\text{B}_2$, C. Vitamin $\text{B}_6$, D. Vitamin $\text{C}$
List-II: I. Pyridoxine, II. Ascorbic acid, III. Thiamine, IV. Riboflavin
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ is Thiamine (III), Vitamin $\text{B}_2$ is Riboflavin (IV), Vitamin $\text{B}_6$ is Pyridoxine (I), and Vitamin $\text{C}$ is Ascorbic acid (II).

question_text: Thiol group is present in:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cysteine ($\text{HS}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(NH}_2\text{)}-\text{COOH}$) contains a free thiol ($-\text{SH}$) side chain, whereas methionine has a thioether ($-\text{SCH}_3$) group and cystine has a disulphide ($-\text{S}-\text{S}-$) linkage.

question_text: Consider the ionisation sequence for aspartic acid with $\text{p}K_1 = 1.88$, $\text{p}K_2 = 3.65$, and $\text{p}K_3 = 9.60$. The $\text{pH}$ (Isoelectric point) of aspartic acid is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: For an acidic amino acid like aspartic acid, the isoelectric point ($\text{pI}$) is the average of the two acidic $\text{p}K_a$ values flanking the neutral zwitterion: $\text{pI} = \frac{\text{p}K_1 + \text{p}K_2}{2} = \frac{1.88 + 3.65}{2} = \frac{5.53}{2} = 2.765 \approx 2.77$.

question_text: Observation of "Ruhemann's purple" is a confirmatory test for the presence of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the ninhydrin test, $\alpha$-amino acids, peptides, and proteins react with ninhydrin to produce a deep blue-violet complex known as Ruhemann's purple.

question_text: Which of the following compounds will behave as reducing sugar in an aqueous $\text{KOH}$ solution?
options: Fructofuranose derivative with an ester group ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$) at the anomeric carbon
subject: Chemistry
solution: An ester group ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$) at the anomeric carbon undergoes base-catalysed hydrolysis in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to regenerate the free hemiketal ($-\text{OH}$ at the anomeric carbon), which opens to a reducing sugar.

question_text: Among the following, the essential amino acid is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Valine is an essential $\alpha$-amino acid that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet, whereas alanine, serine, and aspartic acid are non-essential amino acids.

question_text: The incorrect statement among the following is:
options: The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine.
Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide made up of only $\beta$-D-glucose units.
subject: Chemistry
solution: $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose are diastereomers differing only in configuration at $\text{C}-1$ (anomers), not non-superimposable mirror images (enantiomers). Thus, statement (A) is incorrect.

question_text: Glucose on prolonged heating with $\text{HI}$ gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Prolonged heating of D-glucose with concentrated $\text{HI}$ completely reduces all hydroxyl and carbonyl groups to yield $n$-hexane ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$), proving that all six carbon atoms in glucose are linked in a straight unbranched chain.

question_text: The predominant form of histamine present in human blood is ($\text{p}K_a$, Histidine $= 6.0$):
options: Monoprotonated cation with $-\text{NH}_3^+$ on the aliphatic ethylamine side chain and neutral imidazole ring
Diprotonated dication with both the aliphatic $-\text{NH}_3^+$ and imidazolium ring protonated
Monoprotonated cation with protonated imidazolium ring and neutral $-\text{NH}_2$ side chain
subject: Chemistry
solution: Human blood has $\text{pH} \approx 7.35 - 7.45$. The aliphatic primary amine of histamine ($\text{p}K_a \approx 9.75$) is much more basic than the imidazole ring ($\text{p}K_a \approx 6.0$), so at blood $\text{pH}$ the aliphatic $-\text{NH}_2$ is protonated to $-\text{NH}_3^+$ while the imidazole ring remains neutral.

question_text: Which of the following will not exist in zwitterionic form at $\text{pH} = 7$?
subject: Chemistry
solution: In $N$-acetylalanine, the nitrogen atom is part of an amide ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$) whose lone pair is delocalised into the carbonyl group ($-\text{M}$ effect), making it non-basic and unable to accept a proton to form a zwitterion at $\text{pH} = 7$.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct structure of adenosine?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Adenosine is a purine nucleoside formed by an $N$-glycosidic linkage between the $\text{N}-9$ atom of adenine ($6$-aminopurine) and the $\text{C}-1'$ atom of $\beta$-D-ribofuranose.

question_text: Which of the following will not exist in zwitter ionic form at $\text{pH} = 7$?
subject: Chemistry
solution: The amide nitrogen atom in $N$-acetylalanine is non-basic due to amide resonance, so it cannot be protonated to form a dipolar zwitterion.

question_text: The dipeptide, $\text{Gln-Gly}$, on treatment with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ followed by aqueous work up gives:
options: $N^\alpha$-acetyl-Gln-Gly (acetylated only at the free $\alpha$-amino group of Gln)
Diacetylated product at both the $\alpha$-amino group and side-chain amide of Gln
subject: Chemistry
solution: In $\text{Gln-Gly}$, the nucleophilic N-terminal $-\text{NH}_2$ group of glutamine reacts with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ to form an acetamide ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$), whereas the side-chain primary amide ($-\text{CONH}_2$) of glutamine is non-nucleophilic due to resonance and remains unreacted.

question_text: Among the following, the incorrect statement is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose has an $\alpha(1 \to 2)\beta$-glycosidic linkage, whereas amylose is a linear polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by $\alpha(1 \to 4)$-glycosidic linkages (not $1,2$). Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

question_text: The increasing order of $\text{p}K_a$ of the following amino acids in aqueous solution is: Glycine, Aspartate, Lysine, Arginine.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Isoelectric point / side-chain $\text{p}K_a$ increases with basicity: Aspartate (acidic, $\text{pI} \approx 2.8$) $<$ Glycine (neutral, $\text{pI} \approx 6.0$) $<$ Lysine (basic, $\text{pI} \approx 9.8$) $<$ Arginine (strongly basic guanidinium group, $\text{pI} \approx 10.8$).

question_text: The correct sequence of amino acids present in the tripeptide given below is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Reading from the N-terminus ($-\text{NH}_2$) to the C-terminus ($-\text{COOH}$), the side chains are isopropyl (Valine), hydroxymethyl (Serine), and 1-hydroxyethyl (Threonine), giving the sequence $\text{Val} - \text{Ser} - \text{Thr}$.

question_text:
The correct structure of the product '$\text{P}$' in the following reaction is:
$\text{Asn} - \text{Ser} + (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O (excess)} \xrightarrow{\text{NEt}_3} \text{P}$
subject: Chemistry
solution: Acetic anhydride with $\text{NEt}_3$ acetylates the free N-terminal $-\text{NH}_2$ group of Asn and the side-chain $-\text{OH}$ group of Ser, leaving the side-chain amide ($-\text{CONH}_2$) of Asn intact.

question_text:
The correct match between item I and item II is:
Item I (Compound): a. Lysine, b. Furfural, c. Benzyl alcohol, d. Styrene
Item II (Reagent): p. 1-naphthol, q. Ninhydrin, r. $\text{KMnO}_4$, s. Ceric ammonium nitrate
subject: Chemistry
solution: Lysine (an $\alpha$-amino acid) gives a positive test with ninhydrin ($\text{a} \to \text{q}$); furfural condenses with $\alpha$-naphthol (Molisch test) ($\text{b} \to \text{p}$); alcohols like benzyl alcohol react with ceric ammonium nitrate ($\text{c} \to \text{s}$); and alkenes like styrene are oxidised by $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($\text{d} \to \text{r}$).

question_text: Which of the following tests cannot be used for identifying amino acids?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Barfoed's test is used to distinguish monosaccharides from reducing disaccharides, whereas ninhydrin and xanthoproteic tests are used for amino acids/proteins (and biuret test is for peptide/amide linkages).

question_text: Among the following pyrimidine/heterocyclic compounds, which one is found in RNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Uracil (structure B) is a pyrimidine nucleobase found specifically in RNA (alongside adenine, guanine, and cytosine).

question_text:
The correct match between Item I and Item II is:
Item I (Test): (A) Ester test, (B) Carbylamine test, (C) Phthalein dye test
Item II (Amino acid): (P) Tyr, (Q) Asp, (R) Ser, (S) Lys
subject: Chemistry
solution: Carboxylic acid ($-\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ in Asp) and alcohol ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ in Ser) groups undergo esterification (A $\to$ Q, R); primary amine ($-(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$ in Lys) gives the carbylamine test (B $\to$ S); phenolic $-\text{OH}$ (in Tyr) gives the phthalein dye test (C $\to$ P).

question_text: Among the following compounds most basic amino acid is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Lysine has an aliphatic $\varepsilon$-amino side chain ($\text{pI} \approx 9.8$), making it more basic than neutral serine and asparagine and having a higher isoelectric point than histidine ($\text{pI} \approx 7.6$).

question_text: The correct structure of histidine in a strongly acidic solution ($\text{pH} = 2$) is:
options: Zwitterion with $-\text{NH}_3^+$, $-\text{COO}^-$, and protonated imidazolium ring
Cation with $-\text{NH}_3^+$, $-\text{COOH}$, and protonated imidazole at $\text{N}-1$ (non-aromatic lone pair)
Cation with $-\text{NH}_3^+$, $-\text{COOH}$, and protonated imidazole at $\text{N}-3$ (aromatic lone pair)
Zwitterion with $-\text{NH}_3^+$, $-\text{COO}^-$, and unprotonated imidazole ring
subject: Chemistry
solution: In an acidic solution, basic nitrogen atoms are protonated according to the official JEE answer key (option D).

question_text: Maltose on treatment with dilute $\text{HCl}$ gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose is a reducing disaccharide composed of two D-glucose units joined by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic linkage; acid hydrolysis yields two molecules of D-glucose.

question_text: Fructose and glucose can be distinguished by:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Seliwanoff's test (resorcinol in dilute $\text{HCl}$) distinguishes ketoses like fructose (which rapidly form a cherry-red colour) from aldoses like glucose.

question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about sucrose?
options: It is also named as invert sugar.
The glycosidic linkage is present between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-glucose and $\text{C}_1$ of $\beta$-fructose.
On hydrolysis, it produces glucose and fructose.
subject: Chemistry
solution: In sucrose, the glycosidic linkage connects $\text{C}-1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\text{C}-2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose, not $\text{C}-1$ of $\beta$-fructose. Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.

question_text: The peptide that gives positive ceric ammonium nitrate and carbylamine tests is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Serine ($\text{Ser}$) contains a free hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group that gives a positive ceric ammonium nitrate test, and Lysine ($\text{Lys}$) contains a free primary amino ($-\text{NH}_2$) side chain that gives a positive carbylamine test.

question_text: Amylopectin is composed of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylopectin is a branched polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units featuring $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bonds along chains and $\alpha(1 \to 6)$ glycosidic bonds at branch points.

question_text: Number of stereo centres present in linear and cyclic structures of glucose are respectively:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Open-chain D-glucose has $4$ chiral carbons ($\text{C}-2, \text{C}-3, \text{C}-4, \text{C}-5$), whereas cyclic glucopyranose has $5$ stereocentres because cyclisation creates a new chiral centre at the anomeric $\text{C}-1$ carbon.

question_text: Glucose and Galactose are having identical configuration in all the positions except position:
subject: Chemistry
solution: D-Glucose and D-galactose are $\text{C}-4$ epimers; their configurations are identical at all carbons except $\text{C}-4$.

question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about RNA?
options: It controls the synthesis of protein.
It has always double stranded $\alpha$-helix structure.
It is present in the nucleus of the cell.
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA is typically a single-stranded molecule rather than a double-stranded $\alpha$-helix like DNA. Thus, statement (C) is not true.

question_text: Which of the given statements is incorrect about glycogen?
options: It is present in animal cells.
It is a straight chain polymer similar to amylose.
It is present in some yeast and fungi.
Only $\alpha$-linkages are present in the molecule.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose (similar in structure to amylopectin, with even more branching), not a straight-chain polymer like amylose. Thus, statement (B) is incorrect.

question_text:
Match the following:
(i) Riboflavin — (a) Beriberi
(ii) Thiamine — (b) Scurvy
(iii) Pyridoxine — (c) Cheilosis
(iv) Ascorbic acid — (d) Convulsions
subject: Chemistry
solution: Riboflavin (Vitamin $\text{B}_2$) deficiency causes cheilosis (c); Thiamine (Vitamin $\text{B}_1$) deficiency causes beriberi (a); Pyridoxine (Vitamin $\text{B}_6$) deficiency causes convulsions (d); Ascorbic acid (Vitamin $\text{C}$) deficiency causes scurvy (b).

question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Gluconic acid can form cyclic (acetal/hemiacetal) structure.
Gluconic acid is a dicarboxylic acid.
Gluconic acid is a partial oxidation product of glucose.
Gluconic acid is obtained by oxidation of glucose with $\text{HNO}_3$.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Mild oxidation of glucose (e.g., with $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) selectively oxidises only the $-\text{CHO}$ group to $-\text{COOH}$, forming the monocarboxylic gluconic acid (whereas $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidises both ends to glucaric/saccharic dicarboxylic acid).

question_text: Which of the following statement is not true for glucose?
options: Glucose exists in two crystalline forms $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
Glucose gives Schiff's test for aldehyde.
Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine to give oxime.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Despite having an aldehyde group in its minor open-chain form, glucose does not give a positive Schiff's test (or $\text{NaHSO}_3$ adduct test). Thus, statement (B) is not true.

question_text: Two monomers in maltose are:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose consists of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units joined by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bond.

question_text:
A, B and C are three biomolecules. The results of the tests performed on them are given below:
- A: Molisch's test = Positive, Barfoed's test = Negative, Biuret test = Negative
- B: Molisch's test = Positive, Barfoed's test = Positive, Biuret test = Negative
- C: Molisch's test = Negative, Barfoed's test = Negative, Biuret test = Positive
A, B and C are respectively:
options: A = Glucose, B = Fructose, C = Albumin
A = Lactose, B = Glucose, C = Albumin
A = Lactose, B = Glucose, C = Alanine
A = Lactose, B = Fructose, C = Alanine
subject: Chemistry
solution: A is a carbohydrate (Molisch +) that is a disaccharide (Barfoed -) and not a protein (Biuret -), so A = Lactose; B is a monosaccharide (Molisch +, Barfoed +), so B = Glucose; C is a protein with peptide bonds (Biuret +), so C = Albumin.

question_text:
Consider the following reactions:
(i) $\text{Glucose} + \text{ROH} \xrightarrow{\text{dry HCl}} \text{Acetal}$ ($x$ equiv. of $\text{ROH}$)
(ii) $\text{Glucose} \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}/\text{H}_2} \text{A} \xrightarrow[y\text{ eq. of (CH}_3\text{CO)}_2\text{O}]{} \text{acetyl derivative}$
(iii) $\text{Glucose} \xrightarrow[z\text{ eq. of (CH}_3\text{CO)}_2\text{O}]{} \text{acetyl derivative}$
'$x$', '$y$' and '$z$' in these reactions are respectively:
subject: Chemistry
solution: According to the official JEE answer key, the correct answer is B ($4, 6 \& 5$).

question_text: Sucrose undergoes glycosidic bond cleavage (hydrolysis) to give $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$. When the mixture is treated with Seliwanoff's reagent, the correct observation is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Hydrolysis of sucrose produces glucose and fructose; ketose sugars such as fructose give a characteristic red colour with Seliwanoff's reagent.

question_text: The number of $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ groups present in a tripeptide $\text{Asp} - \text{Glu} - \text{Lys}$ is ______.
subject: Chemistry
solution: In $\text{Asp} - \text{Glu} - \text{Lys}$, there are $2$ peptide amide $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ groups, $1$ C-terminal carboxyl $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ group, and $2$ side-chain carboxyl $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ groups (one on $\text{Asp}$ and one on $\text{Glu}$), giving a total of $5$ $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ groups.

question_text: What are the functional groups present in the structure of maltose?
subject: Chemistry
solution: In maltose, the $\text{C}-1$ of the first glucose ring is locked as a glycosidic acetal, whereas the $\text{C}-1$ of the second glucose ring retains a free hemiacetal group (making maltose a reducing sugar).

question_text: The number of chiral centres present in threonine is ______.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Threonine ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(NH}_2\text{)}-\text{COOH}$) has two stereogenic (chiral) carbon atoms: $\text{C}-2$ ($\alpha$-carbon) and $\text{C}-3$ ($\beta$-carbon bearing $-\text{OH}$).

question_text: Which of the following is not an essential amino acid?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid (synthesized in the body from phenylalanine), whereas valine, leucine, and lysine are essential amino acids.

question_text: The number of chiral carbon(s) present in peptide, $\text{Ile-Arg-Pro}$, is ______.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Isoleucine ($\text{Ile}$) has $2$ chiral carbons ($\alpha$-carbon and *sec*-butyl $\beta$-carbon), Arginine ($\text{Arg}$) has $1$ chiral $\alpha$-carbon, and Proline ($\text{Pro}$) has $1$ chiral $\alpha$-carbon, giving $4$ chiral carbons in total.

question_text: The number of chiral carbons present in sucrose is ______.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose contains $5$ chiral carbons in its $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose unit ($\text{C}-1, \text{C}-2, \text{C}-3, \text{C}-4, \text{C}-5$) and $4$ chiral carbons in its $\beta$-D-fructofuranose unit ($\text{C}-2, \text{C}-3, \text{C}-4, \text{C}-5$), giving $5 + 4 = 9$ chiral carbons in total.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is not true?
options: Lactose contains $\alpha$-glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}_1$ of galactose and $\text{C}_4$ of glucose.
Lactose is a reducing sugar and it gives Fehling's test.
Lactose ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$) is a disaccharide and it contains $8$ hydroxyl groups.
On acid hydrolysis, lactose gives one molecule of D(+)-glucose and one molecule of D(+)-galactose.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Lactose contains a $\beta(1 \to 4)$-glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}-1$ of $\beta$-D-galactose and $\text{C}-4$ of glucose, not an $\alpha$-glycosidic linkage. Thus, statement (A) is not true.

question_text: Out of the following, which type of interaction is responsible for the stabilisation of $\alpha$-helix structure of proteins?
subject: Chemistry
solution: The $\alpha$-helix secondary structure of proteins is stabilised by regular intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the carbonyl oxygen ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$) of one amino acid residue and the amide hydrogen ($-\text{NH}-$) four residues further along the chain.

question_text: Which of the glycosidic linkage between galactose and glucose is present in lactose?
subject: Chemistry
solution: In lactose, the glycosidic bond is a $\beta$-linkage formed between $\text{C}-1$ of $\beta$-D-galactose and $\text{C}-4$ of D-glucose.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct structure of $\alpha$-anomer of maltose?
options: Two $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose rings joined by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bond with $\alpha$-orientation of the free $\text{C}-1'$ $-\text{OH}$ group
Two $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose rings joined by an $\alpha(1 \to 6)$ glycosidic bond
Two $\beta$-D-glucopyranose rings joined by a $\beta(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bond
An $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose ring and a $\beta$-D-glucopyranose ring joined by a $1,2$-linkage
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose consists of two D-glucopyranose units joined by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic linkage; the $\alpha$-anomer has the free anomeric $-\text{OH}$ on the reducing ring oriented $\alpha$ (downward in standard Haworth projection).

question_text: Which of the following vitamins is helpful in blood clotting?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood coagulation (clotting) as a cofactor in the synthesis of clotting factors such as prothrombin.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (a) Sucrose, (b) Lactose, (c) Maltose
List-II: (i) $\beta$-D-Galactose and $\beta$-D-Glucose, (ii) $\alpha$-D-Glucose and $\beta$-D-Fructose, (iii) $\alpha$-D-Glucose and $\alpha$-D-Glucose
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose yields glucose and fructose (ii); lactose yields galactose and glucose (i); maltose yields two units of $\alpha$-D-glucose (iii).

question_text: Seliwanoff test and Xanthoproteic test are used for the identification of ______ and ______ respectively.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Seliwanoff's test identifies ketoses (such as fructose), while the xanthoproteic test (nitration of aromatic rings in proteins with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$) is used to identify proteins containing aromatic amino acids.

question_text: Which among the following pairs of vitamins is stored in our body relatively for longer duration?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Fat-soluble vitamins (such as Vitamin A and Vitamin D) are stored in the liver and adipose tissue for longer durations, whereas water-soluble vitamins (thiamine, ascorbic acid) are readily excreted in urine.

question_text: The secondary structure of protein is stabilised by:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Secondary structures ($\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet) of proteins are stabilised by hydrogen bonds formed between $-\text{NH}-$ and $>\text{C}=\text{O}$ groups of the peptide backbone.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct structure of tyrosine?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Standard L-tyrosine is 2-amino-3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)propanoic acid, having a *para*-hydroxyphenyl group attached to the $\beta$-carbon of alanine (structure D).

question_text:
$\text{Sucrose } (\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}) + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Enzyme A}} \text{Glucose } (\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6) + \text{Fructose } (\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6)$
$\text{Glucose } (\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6) \xrightarrow{\text{Enzyme B}} 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2\text{CO}_2$
In the above reactions, Enzyme A and Enzyme B respectively are:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose is catalysed by invertase (sucrase), and fermentation of glucose into ethanol and $\text{CO}_2$ is catalysed by zymase.

question_text: Fructose is an example of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: D-Fructose has six carbon atoms ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) and a keto group at $\text{C}-2$, classifying it as a ketohexose.

question_text: A non-reducing sugar A hydrolyses to give two reducing monosaccharides. Sugar A is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide that hydrolyses to give two reducing monosaccharides: D-glucose and D-fructose.

question_text: Deficiency of vitamin K causes:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin K is required for blood coagulation; its deficiency delays clotting, leading to an increase in blood clotting time.

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Amylose is a branched chain polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylose is an unbranched (linear) chain polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose linked by $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ bonds, whereas amylopectin is branched. Thus, statement (A) is incorrect.

question_text: The correct structure of Ruhemann's Purple, the compound formed in the reaction of Ninhydrin with proteins/amino acids, is represented by option:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Reaction of ninhydrin with an $\alpha$-amino acid liberates $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{CO}_2$, and an aldehyde, and the resulting amino-indanedione condenses with a second ninhydrin molecule to form the purple anion Ruhemann's purple (option D).

question_text: Thiamine and pyridoxine are also known respectively as:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Thiamine is Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ and pyridoxine is Vitamin $\text{B}_6$.

question_text: The water soluble protein is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Albumins are globular proteins soluble in water, whereas fibrin, myosin, and collagen are insoluble fibrous proteins.

question_text: Which one of the following is the correct structure for cytosine?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cytosine is $4$-aminopyrimidin-$2(1H)$-one (structure C), present in both DNA and RNA.

question_text: Which one among the following chemical tests is used to distinguish monosaccharide from disaccharide?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Barfoed's reagent (acidic copper acetate) is reduced rapidly ($1-2\text{ min}$) by monosaccharides to give a brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate, whereas reducing disaccharides react much more slowly.

question_text: The compound 'A' (thymine) is a complementary base of ______ in DNA strands.
subject: Chemistry
solution: In double-stranded DNA, thymine ($\text{T}$) pairs specifically with adenine ($\text{A}$) via two hydrogen bonds.

question_text: Compound A gives D-Galactose and D-Glucose on hydrolysis. The compound A is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Lactose is a disaccharide composed of $\beta$-D-galactose and D-glucose units joined by a $\beta(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic linkage; hydrolysis yields one molecule each of D-galactose and D-glucose.

question_text: The total number of negative charge in the tetrapeptide, $\text{Gly-Glu-Asp-Tyr}$, at $\text{pH } 12.5$ will be _____ (Integer answer)
subject: Chemistry
solution: At $\text{pH } 12.5$ (strongly basic medium), all acidic groups lose a proton ($\text{H}^+$) to form negatively charged anions: 1 from the $\gamma$-carboxyl group of $\text{Glu}$, 1 from the $\beta$-carboxyl group of $\text{Asp}$, 1 from the phenolic $\text{-OH}$ group of $\text{Tyr}$, and 1 from the C-terminal $\text{-COOH}$ group of $\text{Tyr}$. Thus, the total number of negative charges is $4$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Sucrose is a disaccharide and a non-reducing sugar.
Reason (R): Sucrose involves glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}_1$ of $\beta$-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\alpha$-fructose.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the true explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the true explanation of (A).
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide composed of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-fructose held together by a glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\beta$-fructose. Hence, Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

question_text: Out of following isomeric forms of uracil, which one is present in RNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Uracil exists predominantly in the diketo (lactam) tautomeric form (option A) in RNA.

question_text: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is a disaccharide of $\alpha$-D-$(+)$-glucose and $\beta$-D-$(-)$-fructose. Upon hydrolysis, it yields an equimolar mixture of $\alpha$-D-$(+)$-glucose and $\beta$-D-$(-)$-fructose.

question_text: Which one of the following tests used for the identification of functional groups in organic compounds does not use copper reagent?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Seliwanoff's test uses resorcinol and concentrated $\text{HCl}$ to detect ketohexoses. Biuret, Barfoed's, and Benedict's tests all use $\text{Cu(II)}$ reagents.

question_text: Which one of the following compounds contains $\beta$-$\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ glycosidic linkage?
subject: Chemistry
solution: In lactose, the glycosidic linkage is formed between $\text{C}_1$ of $\beta$-D-galactose and $\text{C}_4$ of $\beta$-D-glucose ($\beta$-$\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ glycosidic linkage).

question_text: Which of the following is NOT an example of fibrous protein ?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Albumin is a water-soluble globular protein, whereas keratin, myosin, and collagen are water-insoluble fibrous proteins.

question_text: A peptide synthesized by the reactions of one molecule each of Glycine, Leucine, Aspartic acid and Histidine will have _____ peptide linkages.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Four amino acid molecules condense to form a tetrapeptide containing $4 - 1 = 3$ peptide linkages ($\text{-CONH-}$).

question_text: A polysaccharide '$\text{X}$' on boiling with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $393\text{ K}$ under $2$–$3\text{ atm}$ pressure yields '$\text{Y}$'. '$\text{Y}$' on treatment with bromine water gives gluconic acid. '$\text{X}$' contains $\beta$-glycosidic linkages only. Compound '$\text{X}$' is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cellulose is a linear polysaccharide of $\beta$-D-glucose units joined exclusively by $\beta(1 \rightarrow 4)$ glycosidic linkages. On hydrolysis with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $393\text{ K}$ and $2$–$3\text{ atm}$, it yields D-glucose ($\text{Y}$), which is oxidized by bromine water to gluconic acid.

question_text: In alanylglycylleucylalanylvaline the number of peptide linkages is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: There are $5$ amino acid residues (Ala, Gly, Leu, Ala, Val) in the pentapeptide sequence, so the number of peptide linkages is $5 - 1 = 4$.

question_text:
How many of the given compounds will give a positive Biuret test?
Glycine, Glycylalanine, Tripeptide, Biuret
subject: Chemistry
solution: According to the official JEE answer key, $2$ compounds (Tripeptide and Biuret; note that dipeptides like glycylalanine generally do not give a positive biuret test as at least two peptide bonds / three amino acid residues are required, though some keys count Glycylalanine and Tripeptide) give a positive Biuret test.

question_text: The number of oxygen present in a nucleotide formed from a base, that is present only in RNA is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: The base present only in RNA is uracil ($2$ oxygens). Combined with $\beta$-D-ribose sugar ($4$ oxygens in the nucleotide) and a phosphate group ($3$ oxygens attached to phosphorus), the uridine monophosphate nucleotide contains $2 + 4 + 3 = 9$ oxygen atoms.

question_text: Which one of the following is a water soluble vitamin, that is not excreted easily?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Water-soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in the diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored in our body, except Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$, which is stored in the liver and not excreted easily.

question_text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I: Maltose has two $\alpha$-D-glucose units linked at $\text{C}_1$ and $\text{C}_4$ and is a reducing sugar.
Statement II: Maltose has two monosaccharides: $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose linked at $\text{C}_1$ and $\text{C}_6$ and it is a non-reducing sugar.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose is composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units in which $\text{C}_1$ of one glucose is linked to $\text{C}_4$ of another glucose unit. Since a free hemiacetal group is present at $\text{C}_1$ of the second glucose unit, it is a reducing sugar. Hence, Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

question_text: Stability of $\alpha$-Helix structure of proteins depends upon
subject: Chemistry
solution: The $\alpha$-helix structure of proteins is stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the $\text{>C=O}$ and $\text{-NH-}$ groups of adjacent turns of the polypeptide chain.

question_text: When sugar '$\text{X}$' is boiled with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in alcoholic solution, two isomers '$\text{A}$' and '$\text{B}$' are formed. '$\text{A}$' on oxidation with $\text{HNO}_3$ yields saccharic acid whereas '$\text{B}$' is laevorotatory. The compound '$\text{X}$' is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$) on acidic hydrolysis gives equimolar amounts of D-glucose ($\text{A}$) and laevorotatory D-fructose ($\text{B}$). D-Glucose on oxidation with $\text{HNO}_3$ yields saccharic acid.

question_text: $2.5\text{ g}$ of protein containing only glycine ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$) is dissolved in water to make $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. The osmotic pressure of this solution at $300\text{ K}$ is found to be $5.03 \times 10^{-3}\text{ bar}$. The total number of glycine units present in the protein is _____ (Given: $R = 0.083\text{ L bar K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
subject: Chemistry
solution:
$$\pi = C R T \implies 5.03 \times 10^{-3} = \left(\frac{2.5 \times 1000}{M_{\text{protein}} \times 500}\right) \times 0.083 \times 300$$
$$M_{\text{protein}} = 24751.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$$
Molar mass of glycine ($\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$) $= 75\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Number of glycine units $= \frac{24751.5}{75} \approx 330$.

question_text:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Zymase}} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{NaOI}} \text{B} + \text{CHI}_3$
The number of carbon atoms present in the product $\text{B}$ is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Zymase}} 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH (A)} + 2\text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{NaOI}} \text{CHI}_3 + \text{HCOO}^-\text{Na}^+ \text{ (B)}$$
Product $\text{B}$ is sodium formate ($\text{HCOONa}$), which contains $1$ carbon atom.

question_text: Sugar moiety in DNA and RNA molecules respectively are
subject: Chemistry
solution: DNA contains $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose sugar, whereas RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose sugar.

question_text: The structure of protein that is unaffected by heating is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: During thermal denaturation of proteins, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures are disrupted, while the primary structure (the sequence of amino acids linked by covalent peptide bonds) remains intact.

question_text: During the denaturation of proteins, which of these structures will remain intact?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Denaturation breaks weak hydrogen bonds and non-covalent interactions responsible for secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures, leaving the covalent peptide bonds of the primary structure intact.

question_text: Glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\beta$-fructose is found in
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is formed by a glycosidic bond between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose.

question_text: Which of the following is reducing sugar?
options: Pyranose sugar with free hemiacetal $\text{-OH}$ group at $\text{C}_1$
Methyl glycoside of pyranose sugar ($\text{-OCH}_3$ at $\text{C}_1$)
Furanose glycoside with $\text{-OCH}_3$ at anomeric carbon
subject: Chemistry
solution: Carbohydrates having a free hemiacetal or hemiketal $\text{-OH}$ group at the anomeric carbon can open to form an aldehyde/ketone and reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent. Structure (A) has a free $\text{-OH}$ group at the anomeric carbon, making it a reducing sugar.

question_text: Animal starch is the other name of
subject: Chemistry
solution: Glycogen is a highly branched polysaccharide of $\alpha$-D-glucose stored in animals and is commonly known as animal starch.

question_text: A sugar '$\text{X}$' dehydrates very slowly under acidic condition to give furfural which on further reaction with resorcinol gives the coloured product after sometime. Sugar '$\text{X}$' is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Acidic dehydration of an aldopentose ($5$-carbon sugar) yields furfural, which condenses slowly with resorcinol (Seliwanoff's reagent) to give a cherry-red coloured product.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
A. $\text{Glucose} + \text{HI}$
B. $\text{Glucose} + \text{Br}_2\text{ water}$
C. $\text{Glucose} + \text{acetic anhydride}$
D. $\text{Glucose} + \text{HNO}_3$
List-II
I. Gluconic acid
II. Glucose pentaacetate
III. Saccharic acid
IV. Hexane
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
subject: Chemistry
solution:
A. $\text{Glucose} + \text{HI} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{n-Hexane (IV)}$
B. $\text{Glucose} + \text{Br}_2\text{ water} \rightarrow \text{Gluconic acid (I)}$
C. $\text{Glucose} + \text{acetic anhydride} \rightarrow \text{Glucose pentaacetate (II)}$
D. $\text{Glucose} + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Saccharic acid (III)}$

question_text: For the below given cyclic hemiacetal ($\text{X}$), the correct pyranose structure is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Converting the Fischer cyclic hemiacetal projection ($\text{X}$) into the Haworth pyranose projection places groups on the left in the Fischer projection pointing UP and groups on the right pointing DOWN, which corresponds to structure (D).

question_text:
The formulas of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ for the following reaction sequence are
$$\text{Fructose} \xrightarrow{\text{HCN}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) HI/P}]{\text{(i) NaBH}_4} \text{B}$$
subject: Chemistry
solution: Fructose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) reacts with $\text{HCN}$ to form a cyanohydrin, which upon hydrolysis gives a $7$-carbon polyhydroxy carboxylic acid $\text{A}$ ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_{14}\text{O}_8$). (Note: According to the official JEE key, reduction with $\text{NaBH}_4$ followed by $\text{HI/P}$ gives $\text{B} = \text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$).

question_text: In a linear tetrapeptide (Constituted with different amino acids), (number of amino acids) $-$ (number of peptide bonds) is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: A linear tetrapeptide has $4$ amino acid residues and $3$ peptide bonds. Therefore, $4 - 3 = 1$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Amylose is insoluble in water.
Reason R: Amylose is a long linear molecule with more than $200$ glucose units.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylose is the water-soluble component of starch (comprising $15$–$20\%$ of starch), whereas amylopectin is water-insoluble. Thus, Assertion A is false, and Reason R is correct.

question_text: Total number of tripeptides possible by mixing of valine and proline is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: Each of the $3$ positions in a tripeptide can be occupied by either Valine or Proline ($2$ choices per position). Total number of possible tripeptides $= 2^3 = 8$.

question_text:
Match items of Row I with those of Row II.
Row I:
(P) $\alpha$-D-$(+)$-Glucopyranose structure
(Q) $\beta$-D-$(+)$-Glucopyranose structure
(R) $\alpha$-D-$(-)$-Fructofuranose structure
(S) $\beta$-D-$(-)$-Fructofuranose structure
Row II:
(i) $\alpha$-D-$(-)$ Fructofuranose
(ii) $\beta$-D-$(-)$ Fructofuranose
(iii) $\alpha$-D-$(+)$ Glucopyranose
(iv) $\beta$-D-$(+)$ Glucopyranose
Correct match is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Structure P represents $\alpha$-D-$(+)$-glucopyranose (iii), Q represents $\beta$-D-$(+)$-glucopyranose (iv), R represents $\alpha$-D-$(-)$-fructofuranose (i), and S represents $\beta$-D-$(-)$-fructofuranose (ii).

question_text: Number of cyclic tripeptides formed with 2 amino acids $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Due to cyclic symmetry (necklaces of length $3$ with $2$ bead types), the distinct cyclic tripeptides formed from $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are $\text{cyclo-(A-A-A)}$, $\text{cyclo-(A-A-B)}$, $\text{cyclo-(A-B-B)}$, and $\text{cyclo-(B-B-B)}$, giving a total of $4$.

question_text:
Following tetrapeptide can be represented as
(F, L, D, Y, I, Q, P are one letter codes for amino acids)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Reading from the N-terminus (left) to the C-terminus (right), the four amino acid residues are Phenylalanine ($\text{F}$), Leucine ($\text{L}$), Aspartic acid ($\text{D}$), and Tyrosine ($\text{Y}$), giving the sequence $\text{FLDY}$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Ketoses give Seliwanoff's test faster than Aldoses.
Reason (R): Ketoses undergo $\beta$-elimination followed by formation of furfural.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Ketoses dehydrate much faster than aldoses in acidic medium to form $5$-hydroxymethylfurfural (not furfural directly via $\beta$-elimination, which occurs for aldoses), giving a rapid red colour with resorcinol. Thus, (A) is true and (R) is false.

question_text: A short peptide on complete hydrolysis produces 3 moles of glycine ($\text{G}$), two moles of leucine ($\text{L}$) and two moles of valine ($\text{V}$) per mole of peptide. The number of peptide linkages in it are _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: Total number of amino acid residues $= 3 + 2 + 2 = 7$. Number of peptide linkages $= 7 - 1 = 6$.

question_text: A protein '$\text{X}$' with molecular weight of $70,000\text{ u}$, on hydrolysis gives amino acids. One of these amino acid is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Complete hydrolysis of proteins yields only $\alpha$-amino acids (where both $\text{-NH}_2$ and $\text{-COOH}$ are attached to the same $\alpha$-carbon). Only option (B) (Leucine) is an $\alpha$-amino acid.

question_text: Compound $\text{A}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5$, gives a tetraacetate with $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$ and oxidation of $\text{A}$ with $\text{Br}_2\text{-H}_2\text{O}$ gives an acid, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_6$. Reduction of $\text{A}$ with $\text{HI}$ gives isopentane. The possible structure of $\text{A}$ is:
options: Branched aldopentose with cyclic hemiacetal ring
subject: Chemistry
solution: Formation of a tetraacetate with $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$ indicates four $\text{-OH}$ groups; oxidation with $\text{Br}_2\text{-H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_6$ indicates an aldehyde ($\text{-CHO}$) group; reduction with $\text{HI}$ to isopentane indicates a branched $5$-carbon skeleton. Structure (C) satisfies all these conditions.

question_text: The correct representation in six membered pyranose form for the following sugar $[\text{X}]$ is
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the given Fischer projection of sugar $[\text{X}]$, the $\text{-OH}$ groups at $\text{C}_2$ and $\text{C}_3$ are on the left (pointing UP in the Haworth projection, cis to each other), and the $\text{-OH}$ group at $\text{C}_4$ is on the right (pointing DOWN, anti to $\text{C}_3\text{-OH}$). Thus, option (B) is correct.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): $\alpha$-halocarboxylic acid on reaction with dil. $\text{NH}_3$ gives good yield of $\alpha$-amino carboxylic acid whereas the yield of amines is very low when prepared from alkyl halides.
Reason (R): Amino acids exist in zwitter ion form in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true statements, but the good yield of $\alpha$-amino acids from $\alpha$-halocarboxylic acids is due to the electron-withdrawing effect of the carboxylate group reducing over-alkylation, rather than zwitterion formation itself. Hence, (B) is correct.

question_text: All structures given below are of vitamin C. Most stable of them is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) exists most stably in the conjugated enediol form (A), which is stabilized by conjugation with the lactone carbonyl group and intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

question_text:
Sulphur ($\text{S}$) containing amino acids from the following are:
(a) isoleucine
(b) cysteine
(c) lysine
(d) methionine
(e) glutamic acid
subject: Chemistry
solution: Among the given amino acids, cysteine (contains a thiol $\text{-SH}$ group) and methionine (contains a thioether $\text{-S-CH}_3$ group) contain sulphur. Hence, (b) and (d) are correct.

question_text: The one that does not stabilize $2^{\circ}$ and $3^{\circ}$ structures of proteins is
subject: Chemistry
solution: The main forces which stabilize the $2^{\circ}$ and $3^{\circ}$ structures of proteins are hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages ($\text{-S-S-}$), van der Waals, and electrostatic forces of attraction. Peroxide linkages ($\text{-O-O-}$) do not stabilize protein structures.

question_text:
L-isomer of tetrose $\text{X}$ ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_4$) gives positive Schiff's test and has two chiral carbons. On acetylation '$\text{X}$' yields triacetate. '$\text{X}$' also undergoes following reactions.
$$\text{'A'} \xleftarrow{\text{HNO}_3} \text{'X'} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{'B'}$$
(where both 'A' and 'B' are chiral compounds)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Since '$\text{X}$' is an L-aldotetrose that yields optically active (chiral) aldaric acid '$\text{A}$' upon $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidation and a chiral alditol '$\text{B}$' upon $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduction (unlike erythrose, which forms meso compounds), '$\text{X}$' must be L-threose (option B).

question_text:
Number of compounds from the following which will not produce orange red precipitate with Benedict solution is _____
Glucose, maltose, sucrose, ribose, 2-deoxyribose, amylose, lactose
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose (a non-reducing disaccharide) and amylose (a polysaccharide without an appreciable concentration of free reducing hemiacetal ends) do not give a positive Benedict's test. All the others (glucose, maltose, ribose, 2-deoxyribose, lactose) are reducing sugars. Thus, the count is $2$.

question_text: In an oligopeptide named Alanylglycylphenylalanylisoleucine, the number of $sp^2$ hybridised carbons is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: Alanylglycylphenylalanylisoleucine is a tetrapeptide containing $3$ amide carbonyl carbons ($\text{C=O}$), $1$ carboxylic acid carbonyl carbon ($\text{-COOH}$), and $6$ aromatic ring carbons from the phenyl group of phenylalanine. Total $sp^2$ hybridized carbons $= 3 + 1 + 6 = 10$.

question_text: The naturally occurring amino acid that contains only one basic functional group in its chemical structure is
subject: Chemistry
solution: Asparagine contains one basic $\alpha$-amino group ($\text{-NH}_2$) and a neutral amide side chain ($\text{-CONH}_2$, whose nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl and is non-basic). Histidine, arginine, and lysine all have basic nitrogen-containing side chains in addition to their $\alpha$-amino group.

question_text: The number of tripeptides formed by three different amino acids using each amino acid once is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: The number of ways to arrange $3$ distinct amino acids in a linear tripeptide using each once is $3! = 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$.

question_text:

subject: Chemistry
solution:

B. $\text{Glucose} + \text{Br}_2\text{ water} \rightarrow \text{Gluconic acid (I)}$
C. $\text{Glucose} + \text{acetic anhydride} \rightarrow \text{Glucose pentaacetate (II)}$
D. $\text{Glucose} + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Saccharic acid (III)}$

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: DNA has two strands which are complementary to each other.
Statement II: Adenine forms hydrogen bonds with guanine and cytosine forms hydrogen bonds with thymine.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
subject: Chemistry
solution: The two strands of DNA are complementary to each other (Statement I is correct). In DNA, adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with thymine ($\text{A=T}$), and guanine forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine ($\text{G}\equiv\text{C}$) (Statement II is incorrect).

question_text: Type of amino acids obtained by hydrolysis of proteins is :
subject: Chemistry
solution: Proteins are polymers of $\alpha$-amino acids; hence, complete hydrolysis of proteins yields only $\alpha$-amino acids.

question_text: Two nucleotides are joined together by a linkage known as :
subject: Chemistry
solution: Nucleotides are joined together by a phosphodiester linkage between the $5'$ and $3'$ carbon atoms of the pentose sugar.

question_text: Which structure of protein remains intact after coagulation of egg white on boiling?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Coagulation of egg white on boiling is an example of protein denaturation, during which secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures are destroyed, but the primary structure remains intact.

question_text: A compound '$\text{X}$' is acidic and it is soluble in $\text{NaOH}$ solution, but insoluble in $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solution. Compound '$\text{X}$' also gives violet colour with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution. The compound '$\text{X}$' is :
subject: Chemistry
solution: Phenol is a weak acid that dissolves in $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium phenoxide, does not react with weak base $\text{NaHCO}_3$, and gives a characteristic violet colouration with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution.

question_text: Sugar which does not give reddish brown precipitate with Fehling's reagent is :
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because the reducing groups of both glucose ($\text{C}_1$) and fructose ($\text{C}_2$) are involved in glycosidic bond formation, so it does not reduce Fehling's reagent.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
A. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Galactose
B. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\beta$-Glucose
C. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Fructose
D. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\beta$-Fructose
List-II
I. Functional isomers
II. Homologues
III. Anomers
IV. Epimers
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
subject: Chemistry
solution: $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Galactose differ in configuration at $\text{C}_4$, so they are $\text{C}_4$-epimers (IV). $\alpha$-Glucose and $\beta$-Glucose differ in configuration at the anomeric carbon ($\text{C}_1$), so they are anomers (III). Glucose (an aldohexose) and Fructose (a ketohexose) have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) with different functional groups, so they are functional isomers (I).

question_text: From the vitamins $\text{A}, \text{B}_1, \text{B}_6, \text{B}_{12}, \text{C}, \text{D}, \text{E}$ and $\text{K}$, the number of vitamins that can be stored in our body is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: Fat-soluble vitamins ($\text{A}, \text{D}, \text{E}, \text{K}$) are stored in the liver and adipose tissues, and among water-soluble vitamins, Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ is also stored in the body. Thus, a total of $5$ vitamins ($\text{A}, \text{D}, \text{E}, \text{K}, \text{B}_{12}$) can be stored in our body.

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: Amylose is a branched chain polymer of glucose
Glycogen is called as animal starch
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylose is a long unbranched (linear) chain polymer of $\alpha$-D-$(+)$-glucose units held together by $\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ glycosidic linkages. Amylopectin is the branched-chain component of starch. Hence, statement (A) is incorrect.

question_text: The correct statement about the given structure of sucrose is :
options: Both rings are in pyranose form
Glycosidic linkage is present between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose
It has a free hemiacetal group
subject: Chemistry
solution: In sucrose, $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose and $\beta$-D-fructofuranose are joined by a glycosidic linkage between $\text{C}_1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\text{C}_2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose.

question_text: The number of chiral carbons present in sucrose is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: In cyclic sucrose, the $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose ring contains $5$ chiral carbons ($\text{C}_1, \text{C}_2, \text{C}_3, \text{C}_4, \text{C}_5$) and the $\beta$-D-fructofuranose ring contains $4$ chiral carbons ($\text{C}_2, \text{C}_3, \text{C}_4, \text{C}_5$). Total chiral carbons $= 5 + 4 = 9$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Fructose does not contain an aldehydic group but still reduces Tollens' reagent.
Statement II: In the presence of base, fructose undergoes rearrangement to give glucose.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
subject: Chemistry
solution: Fructose is a ketohexose without a free aldehydic group, yet it reduces Tollens' reagent because in the basic medium of Tollens' reagent, it undergoes Lobry de Bruyn–Alberda van Ekenstein tautomerization (rearrangement via an enediol intermediate) to form glucose and mannose.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): $\text{NH}_2$ group of aniline is acetylated before carrying out nitration.
Reason (R): The acetylated product is less reactive towards electrophilic substitution than aniline and prevents oxidation as well as poly-substitution.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Direct nitration of aniline leads to tarry oxidation products and significant meta-nitration due to anilinium ion formation. Protecting the $\text{-NH}_2$ group by acetylation reduces the activating effect via resonance into the carbonyl group, yielding predominantly p-nitroacetanilide.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In starch, amylose is water soluble and amylopectin is water insoluble.
Statement II: Amylose is a branched chain polymer of glucose while amylopectin is a linear chain polymer of glucose.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylose is water-soluble and linear ($\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ linkages), whereas amylopectin is water-insoluble and branched ($\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ and $\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_6$ linkages). Thus, Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (Vitamin)
A. Vitamin $\text{B}_1$
B. Vitamin $\text{B}_2$
C. Vitamin $\text{B}_6$
D. Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$

C. Vitamin $\text{B}_6$ $\rightarrow$ Convulsions (II)
