question_text: Identify the correct statement among the following:
options: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives equimolar mixture of D-$(+)$-glucose and D-$(-)$-fructose
Glycogen is a linear polymer of $\beta$-D-glucose
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose is dextrorotatory ($+66.5^{\circ}$), and upon hydrolysis it gives an equimolar mixture of dextrorotatory D-$(+)$-glucose ($+52.5^{\circ}$) and laevorotatory D-$(-)$-fructose ($-92.4^{\circ}$).

question_text:
The number of essential amino acids among the following is _____
Valine, Glycine, Alanine, Leucine, Lysine, Proline, Histidine
subject: Chemistry
solution: Among the listed amino acids, Valine, Leucine, Lysine, and Histidine are essential amino acids ($4$ in total), whereas Glycine, Alanine, and Proline are non-essential amino acids.

question_text: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Lysine has two amino ($\text{-NH}_2$) groups and one carboxyl ($\text{-COOH}$) group, making it a basic amino acid.

question_text: The number of tripeptides formed using three different amino acids $\text{A}, \text{B}$ and $\text{C}$ (repetition allowed) is _____
subject: Chemistry
solution: With repetition allowed, each of the $3$ positions in a tripeptide can be filled in $3$ ways, giving $3^3 = 27$ possible tripeptides.

question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about RNA?
options: It controls the synthesis of protein.
It has always double stranded $\alpha$-helix structure.
It is present in the nucleus of the cell.
subject: Chemistry
solution: RNA molecules are generally single-stranded (sometimes folding back on themselves to form localized helical regions) and do not always have a double-stranded $\alpha$-helix structure.

question_text: The peptide that gives positive ceric ammonium nitrate and carbylamine tests is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Ceric ammonium nitrate test detects alcoholic $\text{-OH}$ groups (present in Serine, $\text{Ser}$), and the carbylamine test detects primary aliphatic amine groups ($\text{-NH}_2$, present at the N-terminus and in the side chain of Lysine, $\text{Lys}$). Thus, $\text{Ser-Lys}$ gives both tests positively.

question_text: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose lacks a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group and is therefore a non-reducing sugar.

question_text: Amylopectin is composed of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Amylopectin is a branched-chain polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose units in which the linear chain is formed by $\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ glycosidic linkages and branching occurs via $\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_6$ glycosidic linkages.

question_text: Glucose and Galactose are having identical configuration in all the positions except position:
subject: Chemistry
solution: D-Glucose and D-Galactose are $\text{C-4}$ epimers, differing in configuration only at the $\text{C-4}$ chiral centre.

question_text: Maltose on treatment with dilute $\text{HCl}$ gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose is composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units; upon acidic hydrolysis with dilute $\text{HCl}$, it yields two moles of D-glucose.

question_text:
The correct structure of product '$\text{P}$' in the following reaction is:
$$\text{Asn-Ser} + (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{NEt}_3} \text{P (excess)}$$
options: Diacetylated product at N-terminal $\text{-NH}_2$ and Serine $\text{-OH}$
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the dipeptide $\text{Asn-Ser}$, excess acetic anhydride in the presence of $\text{NEt}_3$ acetylates the free nucleophilic primary amine group at the N-terminus of Asparagine and the primary alcoholic $\text{-OH}$ group of Serine, leaving the less nucleophilic amide group of Asparagine unacetylated.

question_text: Among the following compounds, which one is found in RNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Uracil is the pyrimidine base found in RNA in place of thymine.

question_text: The correct sequence of amino acids present in the tripeptide given below is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Reading from the N-terminus ($\text{-NH}_2$) to the C-terminus ($\text{-COOH}$), the side chains correspond to Valine ($\text{-CH(CH}_3)_2$), Serine ($\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$), and Threonine ($\text{-CH(OH)CH}_3$), giving $\text{Val - Ser - Thr}$.

question_text:
The increasing order of $\text{p}K_a$ of the following amino acids in aqueous solution is:
Gly, Asp, Lys, Arg
subject: Chemistry
solution: Aspartic acid ($\text{Asp}$) is acidic (lowest $\text{p}K_a$ / $\text{pI} \approx 2.8$), Glycine ($\text{Gly}$) is neutral ($\text{pI} \approx 6.0$), Lysine ($\text{Lys}$) is basic ($\text{pI} \approx 9.7$), and Arginine ($\text{Arg}$) is the most strongly basic due to its guanidinium group ($\text{pI} \approx 10.8$). Hence, $\text{Asp} < \text{Gly} < \text{Lys} < \text{Arg}$.

question_text: Which of the following compounds is NOT a reducing sugar?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose has no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group and therefore does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent.

question_text: Glucose on prolonged heating with $\text{HI}$ gives:
subject: Chemistry
solution: On prolonged heating with $\text{HI}$, glucose is completely reduced to n-hexane, suggesting that all six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.

question_text: Which of the following will NOT give test for $\text{N}$ in Lassaigne's test?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{-NH}_2$) does not contain any carbon atoms, so it cannot form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$) upon fusion with sodium metal and fails Lassaigne's test for nitrogen.

question_text: The predominant form of histamine present in human blood is ($\text{pH} = 7.4$):
options: Monoprotonated cation at the aliphatic primary amino group
Monoprotonated cation at the imidazole ring nitrogen
subject: Chemistry
solution: At physiological $\text{pH } 7.4$, the more basic aliphatic primary amine side chain ($\text{p}K_a \approx 9.8$) of histamine is protonated ($\text{-NH}_3^+$), while the less basic imidazole ring ($\text{p}K_a \approx 6.0$) remains neutral.

question_text: Among the following, the essential amino acid is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Valine cannot be synthesized in the human body and must be obtained through diet; hence, it is an essential amino acid.

question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Insulin maintains sugar level in the blood of a human body.
Ovalbumin is a simple food reserve in egg white.
Blood proteins thrombin and fibrinogen are involved in blood clotting.
Denaturation makes the proteins more active.
subject: Chemistry
solution: During denaturation, proteins lose their native $3\text{D}$ structure and consequently lose their biological activity rather than becoming more active.

question_text: Thiol group is present in:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cysteine ($\text{HS-CH}_2\text{-CH(NH}_2\text{)-COOH}$) contains a thiol ($\text{-SH}$) functional group.

question_text: Which of the vitamins given below is water soluble?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin $\text{B}$ complex and Vitamin $\text{C}$ are water-soluble vitamins, whereas Vitamins $\text{A}, \text{D}, \text{E},$ and $\text{K}$ are fat-soluble.

question_text: Synthesis of each molecule of glucose in photosynthesis involves:
subject: Chemistry
solution: In the Calvin cycle of photosynthesis, synthesis of $1$ molecule of glucose requires $18$ molecules of $\text{ATP}$ and $12$ molecules of $\text{NADPH}$.

question_text: Which of the following is a zwitter ion?
subject: Chemistry
solution: $\text{H}_3\text{N}^+\text{-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-$ is a dipolar ion (zwitter ion) containing both a positively charged ammonium group and a negatively charged carboxylate group within the same neutral molecule.

question_text: Accumulation of which of the following molecules in the muscles occurs as a result of vigorous exercise?
subject: Chemistry
solution: During vigorous exercise under anaerobic conditions in muscles, pyruvic acid is reduced to L-lactic acid, causing muscle fatigue.

question_text: Which of the following bases is NOT present in DNA?
subject: Chemistry
solution: DNA contains Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, and Thymine; Uracil is present in RNA instead of DNA.

question_text: Dinucleotide is obtained by joining two nucleotides together by phosphodiester linkage. Between which carbon atoms of pentose sugars of nucleotides are these linkages present?
subject: Chemistry
solution: In nucleic acids, two nucleotides are connected via a phosphodiester bond between the $3'$-hydroxyl group of one pentose sugar and the $5'$-phosphate group of the next pentose sugar.

question_text: Which of the following statements about cellulose is correct?
options: It is a branched polymer of $\alpha$-D-glucose
It is a linear polymer of $\beta$-D-glucose
It is readily digested by human enzymes
It gives blue colour with iodine
subject: Chemistry
solution: Cellulose is a straight-chain polysaccharide composed exclusively of $\beta$-D-glucose units joined by $\text{C}_1$-$\text{C}_4$ glycosidic linkages.

question_text: Deficiency of Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ causes the disease:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Deficiency of Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ (thiamine) causes Beri-Beri (loss of appetite and retarded growth).

question_text: What is the monomer of polypeptide?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Polypeptides and proteins are condensation polymers formed from $\alpha$-amino acid monomers linked by peptide bonds.

question_text: Which of the following is an example of globular protein?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Insulin and albumins are common examples of globular proteins, whereas keratin, myosin, and collagen are fibrous proteins.

question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about fructose?
options: It exists in pyranose form in sucrose
It does not reduce Fehling's solution
subject: Chemistry
solution: Fructose is a natural monosaccharide containing six carbon atoms and a ketonic functional group at $\text{C-2}$, making it a ketohexose.

question_text: The change in optical rotation of freshly prepared solution of glucose is known as:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Mutarotation is the spontaneous change in the specific optical rotation of an optically active compound (such as $\alpha$-D-glucose or $\beta$-D-glucose) in aqueous solution due to equilibration between its anomers via the open-chain form.

question_text: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Both DNA and RNA contain chiral D-pentose sugars (D-2-deoxyribose in DNA and D-ribose in RNA) possessing multiple stereocentres, which is the primary source of chirality in nucleic acids.

question_text: A student is given one compound among the following cyclic structures (A, B, C, D) that gives a positive test with Tollens' reagent. The compound is:
options: Compound A (cyclic acetal / glycoside without free anomeric $-\text{OH}$)
Compound B (cyclic ether with methoxy group at non-anomeric position)
Compound C (cyclic hemiacetal in equilibrium with open-chain hydroxy-aldehyde)
Compound D (cyclic ether with non-anomeric $-\text{OH}$ group)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Tollens' reagent is reduced by free aldehydes/hemiacetals that can ring-open in aqueous solution. Compound C is a cyclic hemiacetal that exists in equilibrium with its open-chain aldehyde form and therefore gives a positive Tollens' test (note: the official answer key for the printed variant lists D).

question_text: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Permuting three distinct amino acids (ala, gly, val) each used once gives $3! = 6$ tripeptide sequences: ala-gly-val, ala-val-gly, gly-ala-val, gly-val-ala, val-ala-gly, and val-gly-ala (official key: C).

question_text: In the given pentapeptide, find out an essential amino acid ($\text{Y}$) and the sequence present in the pentapeptide:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Among the constituent amino acids (Threonine, Serine, Aspartic acid, Glycine, Alanine), Threonine is an essential amino acid ($\text{Y}$), and the pentapeptide sequence from N-terminus to C-terminus is $\text{Thr-Ser-Asp-Gly-Ala}$.

question_text: Structures of four disaccharides are given below. Among the given disaccharides, the non-reducing sugar is:
options: Cellobiose / Lactose ($\beta(1 \to 4)$ linkage with free hemiacetal)
Sucrose ($\alpha(1 \to 2)\beta$ linkage between $\text{C}-1$ of glucose and $\text{C}-2$ of fructose)
subject: Chemistry
solution: Sucrose (structure 3) is a non-reducing disaccharide because both anomeric carbons ($\text{C}-1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\text{C}-2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose) are involved in the glycosidic linkage, leaving no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group.

question_text:
Match List-I (Vitamin) with List-II (Name):
List-I: A. Vitamin $\text{B}_1$, B. Vitamin $\text{B}_2$, C. Vitamin $\text{B}_6$, D. Vitamin $\text{C}$
List-II: I. Pyridoxine, II. Ascorbic acid, III. Thiamine, IV. Riboflavin
subject: Chemistry
solution: Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ is Thiamine (III), Vitamin $\text{B}_2$ is Riboflavin (IV), Vitamin $\text{B}_6$ is Pyridoxine (I), and Vitamin $\text{C}$ is Ascorbic acid (II).

question_text: Identify the correct pair having amino acid ($\text{A}$) and the hormone ($\text{B}$) that is iodinated derivative of the amino acid ($\text{A}$). ($\text{T}$ and $\text{Y}$ represent one-letter codes for amino acids):
subject: Chemistry
solution: Thyroxine ($\text{T}_4$) is a thyroid hormone synthesized as an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine, whose one-letter code is $\text{Y}$.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Maltose has two $\alpha$-D-glucose units linked at $\text{C}_1$ and $\text{C}_4$ and is a non-reducing sugar.
Statement II: Lactose has $\beta$-D-galactose and $\beta$-D-glucose linked at $\text{C}_1$ and $\text{C}_4$ and is a reducing sugar.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
subject: Chemistry
solution: Maltose has a free hemiacetal $-\text{OH}$ on the second glucose ring and is a reducing sugar (Statement I is false). Lactose also has a free hemiacetal group on its glucose unit and is a reducing sugar (Statement II is true).

question_text:
Match List-I (Name of amino acid) with List-II (One-letter symbol / type):
List-I: A. Arginine, B. Aspartic acid, C. Lysine, D. Glutamic acid
List-II: I. D / Non-essential, II. R / Essential, III. E / Non-essential, IV. K / Essential
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Arginine is an essential amino acid with one-letter code $\text{R}$ (A-II); Aspartic acid is non-essential with code $\text{D}$ (B-I); Lysine is essential with code $\text{K}$ (C-IV); Glutamic acid is non-essential with code $\text{E}$ (D-III).

question_text: A D-aldotetrose on oxidation with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ resulted in an optically inactive dicarboxylic acid (*meso*-tartaric acid). The structure of the D-aldotetrose is:
options: L-erythrose ($\text{C}-3$ $-\text{OH}$ on left in Fischer projection)
D-erythrose (both $\text{C}-2$ and $\text{C}-3$ $-\text{OH}$ groups on the right side in Fischer projection)
D-threose ($\text{C}-2$ $-\text{OH}$ on left, $\text{C}-3$ $-\text{OH}$ on right side in Fischer projection)
subject: Chemistry
solution: A D-sugar has $-\text{OH}$ at $\text{C}-3$ on the right. Oxidation of D-erythrose (both $\text{C}-2$ and $\text{C}-3$ $-\text{OH}$ on the right) with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ yields *meso*-tartaric acid, which has an internal plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.

question_text:
Identify the correct statements:
(A) Glucose exists in two anomeric forms.
(B) Anomers of glucose differ in configuration at $\text{C}-1$ in cyclic hemiacetal structure.
(C) Melting point of $\alpha$-anomer of glucose is greater than $\beta$-anomer.
(D) Specific rotation of $\alpha$-anomer is $+19^\circ$ while for $\beta$-anomer is $+112^\circ$.
(E) $\alpha$ and $\beta$-anomers of glucose are prepared by crystallization of saturated glucose solution at $303\text{ K}$ and $371\text{ K}$ respectively.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Statements A, B, and E are correct. Statement C is incorrect because $\beta$-D-glucose ($423\text{ K}$) has a higher melting point than $\alpha$-D-glucose ($419\text{ K}$), and Statement D is reversed ($\alpha$: $+112^\circ$, $\beta$: $+18.7^\circ \approx +19^\circ$).

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The two cyclic forms of D-(+)-glucose ($\alpha$ and $\beta$ anomers differing at $\text{C}_1$ hydroxyl orientation) are two anomers of D-(+)-glucose.
Statement II: The open chain forms of D-glucose and D-fructose contain three similar chiral carbons at $\text{C}_3$, $\text{C}_4$ and $\text{C}_5$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
subject: Chemistry
solution: Both Statement I and Statement II are true: $\alpha$- and $\beta$-D-(+)-glucose differ only at $\text{C}-1$ (anomers), and the open-chain forms of D-glucose and D-fructose share identical stereochemical configurations at $\text{C}-3$, $\text{C}-4$, and $\text{C}-5$.

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement about tertiary structure of proteins:
options: They can be fibrous or globular in structure.
The main forces that stabilize the structure are hydrogen bonding, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces of attraction.
The structure remains intact when exposed to $\text{pH}$ changes.
It represents overall folding of the polypeptide chains.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Tertiary structure of proteins is disrupted (denatured) by changes in $\text{pH}$ or temperature, which break hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and other non-covalent interactions. Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.

question_text:
Match List-I (Amino acid) with List-II (Positive reaction/Test for functional group present in side chain of amino acid):
List-I: A. Glutamine, B. Lysine, C. Tyrosine, D. Serine
List-II: I. Hinsberg's test, II. Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ test, III. Ceric ammonium nitrate test, IV. Hoffmann bromamide degradation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Glutamine has a side-chain amide ($-\text{CONH}_2$) $\to$ Hoffmann bromamide degradation (IV); Lysine has a side-chain primary amine $\to$ Hinsberg's test (I); Tyrosine has a phenolic $-\text{OH}$ $\to$ Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ test (II); Serine has an alcoholic $-\text{OH}$ $\to$ Ceric ammonium nitrate test (III).

question_text:

question_text:
Consider the following reactions on D-glucose:
(i) $\text{HI}, \Delta \longrightarrow n\text{-hexane}$
(ii) $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5 / 10-20\text{ atm} / 773\text{ K} \longrightarrow \text{Benzene}$
(iii) $\text{Benzoyl chloride} / \text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3 \longrightarrow \text{Product (X) (benzophenone)}$
Total number of electrons in the $\pi$ bonds and lone pair of electrons in the product ($\text{X}$) is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Product ($\text{X}$) is benzophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$), which has $7$ $\pi$ bonds ($3$ in each of the two phenyl rings $+ 1$ in $\text{C}=\text{O}$) $= 14$ $\pi$ electrons, plus $2$ lone pairs ($4$ electrons) on the carbonyl oxygen. Total $= 14 + 4 = 18$ electrons.

question_text: The incorrect statement from the following with respect to carbohydrates is:
options: The monosaccharide units obtained from hydrolysis of oligosaccharides are always the same.
Polysaccharides yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis.
D-(+)-glucose exists in equilibrium between open-chain and cyclic forms in aqueous solution.
subject: Chemistry
solution: Hydrolysis of oligosaccharides does not always give identical monosaccharide units—for example, sucrose yields D-glucose and D-fructose, and lactose yields D-galactose and D-glucose. Thus, statement (B) is incorrect.

question_text: Which of the following amino acids will give a violet coloured complex with neutral ferric chloride solution?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ gives a violet/purple complex with phenols. Among the given amino acids, only tyrosine possesses a phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group in its side chain.
